title: The Trophy Case Bowling Ball Swap
crime_description: The championship gold bowling trophy was replaced with a frozen honey-glazed ham.

suspect.name: Bertrand P. Fritterstein, Esq.
suspect.quirk: Speaks in over-the-top, thespian-like monologues, often incorporating made-up etymology

dossier.text: Security footage shows a figure in a bright pink jumpsuit entering the trophy case at 10:40 PM.
An inspection of the trophy case reveals a smudge of golden polish on the handle, matching the color of the stolen trophy.
Eyewitnesses report seeing a man matching the suspect's description near the trophy case around 10:45 PM, muttering something about 'the art of subversion.'

truth_timeline.event: Suspect prepares tools and sneaks in.

lie_plan.cover_story: I was at a charity gala for extreme ironing enthusiasts at the time of the crime.

weak_points.claim: I didn't enter the trophy case, I was merely admiring the decorations.
weak_points.planned_slip: Oh, I mean, I was admiring the, uh, the...the trophy itself.

weak_points.claim: The golden polish smudge must have been left by the previous night's janitorial staff.
weak_points.planned_slip: Yes, yes, I'm sure it's just a coincidence.

weak_points.claim: Those eyewitnesses must have mistaken me for someone else, I was actually at the...the...uh, the snack bar.
weak_points.planned_slip: What? No, no, I was just, uh, discussing the finer points of...of...of subversive snacking.

solution_contradictions: Suspect claimed not to have entered the trophy case, which directly conflicts with fact-1.
Suspect attempted to shift blame to janitorial staff regarding the golden polish, which directly conflicts with fact-2.
